item.title: Prime Minister w/ Q&A | Additional Films and Guests — Wed Oct 21, 7:00 PM — IU Cinema
item.description:
This gripping documentary chronicles Jacinda Ardern navigating unprecedented national tragedies, a volcanic eruption, and a global pandemic as New Zealand’s youngest female leader. By balancing immense political pressure with first-time motherhood, she redefines global leadership through an empathetic yet resolute approach. Packed with raw audio diaries and candid footage, this film delivers a powerful, inspiring portrait of a woman who proved that vulnerability and unyielding strength can rewrite the rules of power. [101 min; documentary; English] A Q&A will follow the screening.
Source: Pillar Arts Community Calendar, Visit Bloomington

item.title: Yonder Mountain String Band — Wed Oct 21, 7:00 PM — Buskirk-Chumley Theater
item.description: Grammy-nominated Yonder Mountain String Band set the tone for a new way forward in acoustic music, carrying bluegrass into rooms and conversations it had never reached before. Nearly three decades later, that same spirit still guides them, alive and present on Good As True (2026), the band’s 12th studio album, arriving March 27th, 2026. The record captures Yonder in full stride. It’s unguarded and in motion, preserving the spark of musicians playing in real time and leaning into everything they have learned along the way. Good As True (2026) digs into communication, the conversations that carry us forward and the ones that fall apart. The things we say, the things we mean, and what gets lost in between. “Brand New Heartache,” the album’s lead single, lives in that fragile moment after a breakup when heartbreak and forward motion exist at the same time. Built on rock-leaning verses and a bluegrass-lifted chorus, it turns loss into motion and sets the tone for the record. From the indeli

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Thu Oct 22 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Thu Oct 22 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Thu Oct 22 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.description:
Affirmation Thursday is a tabling event at the Indiana Memorial Union designed to support students' mental well-being during their first months of the semester. Our organization will hand out positive affirmations to passing students and provide a space for them to write down their thoughts and feelings about their first month of school. The event aims to foster a sense of belonging and encourage students to pause, reflect, and practice self-kindness during a busy and often stressful transition. Participation is free and open to all students, and no sign-up is required. Materials will include affirmation cards, writing supplies, and a table display.
Hosted by: Black Men Evolve

item.title: Taiwan Studies Initiative: Prof. James Lin — Fri Oct 23, 12:00 PM — GLOBAL & INTERNATIONAL STUDIES BUILDING
item.description: In just half a century, Taiwan transformed from an agricultural colony into an economic power, spurred by efforts of the authoritarian Republic of China government in land reform, farmers associations, and improved crop varieties. Yet overlooked is how Taiwan brought these practices to the developing world. In the Global Vanguard elucidates the history and impact of the "Taiwan model" of agrarian development by incorporating how Taiwanese experts took the country's agrarian success and exported it throughout rural communities across Africa and Southeast Asia. Driven by the global Cold War and challenges to the Republic of China's legitimacy, Taiwanese agricultural technicians and scientists shared their practices, which they claimed were better suited for poor, tropical societies in the developing world. item.title: Don't Look Now | Friday Night Frights — Fri Oct 23, 10:00 PM — IU CINEMA
item.description: Adapted from a Daphne du Maurier short story, Don’t Look Now follows John (Donald Sutherland) and Christine (Julie Christie), still grieving over the accidental death of their daughter, as they head to Venice for John's work restoring a church. Soon, Laura meets two sisters who claim to be in touch with the spirit of their dead daughter and the couple must decide what is real, what is supernatural, and what is somewhere in-between. Renowned for innovative editing style, memorable recurring aesthetic motifs, an impressionistic formal style, and nonlinear storytelling that destabilizes the viewer, the film was controversial on its release but is now considered a classic, landing multiples times on Sight and Sound's list of the best films of all time, the BFI list of greatest British films, and was reevaluated by Roget Ebert as an occult-horror classic. Don't Look Now has also inspired filmmakers like Danny Boyle, Lynne Ramsey, Ari Aster, Steven Soderbergh, and many more. [110 min; horror

item.title: Rust Memorial All-Day Singing — Sat Oct 24, 10:00 AM — St. Marks United Methodist Church
item.description:
Singers and the curious are invited to the 21st annual David Rust Memorial All-Day Sacred Harp Singing. The event takes place at St. Mark's United Methodist Church (100 N State Road 46, Bloomington, IN) on Saturday, October 24, 2026 in Bloomington, Indiana. We will sing from 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m., with a traditional potluck dinner on the grounds at noon. Local singers are encouraged to bring a dish to share. We will be singing from both the 2025 revision of The Sacred Harp and The Shenandoah Harmony. Don't worry: Loaner song books will be available. A voluntary donation will be taken to help cover expenses. Learn more along with parking instructions bloomingtonsacredharp.com Other area singings are listed on the website as well, including a Cooper Book singing on Sunday, October 25 at the Leipsic Community Center near Orleans, Indiana.

item.title: And So I Stayed w/Q&A | Additional Films and Guests — Sat Oct 24, 7:00 PM — IU CINEMA
item.description: And So I Stayed is an award-winning documentary by Natalie Pattillo and Daniel A. Nelson about survivors of abuse fighting for their lives and spending years behind bars. It is a moving portrait of Kim, Tanisha, and Nikki, three survivors whose strikingly similar stories are separated by over 30 years. None of them were believed, and each of them was criminalized for fighting back. This film is made for and by survivors. For them and us to feel heard, seen, and believed. item.title: Percussion Ensemble – Kevin Bobo, Joseph Gramley, and John Tafoya, directors — Sun Oct 25, 1:00 PM — Auer Hall
item.description: Enjoy this performance from almost anywhere in the world via LIVE@jacobs! About the Directors Kevin Bobo is professor of music in percussion at the Indiana University Jacobs School of Music, a position he has held since 2007. Prior to his appointment at the Jacobs School, he served as assistant professor of percussion at the University of Kansas (2003-07). He studied percussion with J. C. Combs and Gordon Stout and composition with Greg Woodward and Dana Wilson. Internationally respected as a solo marimba artist, Bobo has performed on five continents. His travels have taken him to Taiwan, Singapore, Argentina, Puerto Rico, Mexico, Australia, Spain, Latvia, Lithuania, France, Italy, the Czech Republic, and nearly 40 states in the United States. As a composer, Bobo’s compositions are performed all over the world, with his solo works frequently appearing on international competition repertoire lists. item.title: Kagemusha | Michael A. McRobbie's Choice — Sun Oct 25, 7:00 PM — IU CINEMA
item.description:
Akira Kurosawa's lauded feudal epic follows the story of a petty thief recruited to impersonate an aging warlord in an effort to keep the warlord safe from attacking competing clans. When the warlord dies, his general reluctantly empowers the imposter to take over as the ruler to maintain their control. But his commitment to his new role is tested when forced to lead "his" troops into battle. Winner of the 1980 Cannes Film Festival Palme d'Or, Kagemusha merges the passion of youthful artistic creation with the genius of a master filmmaker. [162 min; drama, war; Japanese with English subtitles]
Source: IU Cinema, Visit Bloomington

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Mon Oct 26 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Mon Oct 26 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Mon Oct 26 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past
